evidenceAudit.scope: Women at average risk of breast cancer: who to offer screening mammography, how often, when to stop, and when a symptom needs urgent referral instead of screening. Verified against the Saudi PHA Clinical Preventive Guideline 2023 (Saudi Expert Panel recommendation), the USPSTF 2024 recommendation and NICE NG12 for symptomatic referral.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: High-risk screening (MRI, earlier start) criteria not reproduced — specialist service
Saudi national screening programme invitation process not checked

pathophysiology.summary: Breast cancer arises from the epithelium of the ducts or lobules. Screening mammography detects cancers before they are palpable, when treatment is less extensive. It also finds some cancers that would never have caused harm (overdiagnosis) and produces false-positive recalls.
keyMechanisms: Most breast cancers develop over years from in-situ to invasive disease, giving a window for detection.
Mammography detects microcalcification and masses; dense breast tissue lowers sensitivity (USPSTF).
Benefit rises with age-related risk; harms (false positives, overdiagnosis) are highest in younger women.

symptoms: Screening is for women without symptoms.
Ask about breast lump, nipple discharge or retraction, skin change — these need diagnostic referral, not screening.
physicalSigns: Clinical breast examination if symptomatic; axillary nodes.
redFlags: Unexplained breast lump at 30 or over — suspected cancer referral (NICE NG12 1.4.1)
Age 50 or over with unilateral nipple discharge, retraction or other change — suspected cancer referral (NICE 1.4.1)
Skin changes suggesting cancer or unexplained axillary lump at 30 or over — consider urgent referral (NICE 1.4.2)
precipitants: Chest radiotherapy at a young age

differentials.condition: High-risk women (BRCA1/2, chest radiotherapy at a young age, previous breast cancer)
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Not covered by average-risk screening (USPSTF) — specialist pathway.
Diagnostic imaging and referral, not screening.

ruleIn.testName: Breast symptom check and risk history
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Lump, nipple change, skin change; BRCA family history or chest radiotherapy.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Symptomatic → NICE NG12 referral; high risk → specialist pathway.

ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Recall for diagnostic imaging and possible biopsy; most recalls are benign.

clinicalManagement.title: Who and how often
actions: Saudi Expert Panel (PHA 2023): offer mammography to women 40–69 years every 1–2 years (conditional recommendation, low-quality evidence).
75 or older: evidence insufficient for routine screening — individual decision (PHA; USPSTF).

clinicalManagement.title: Shared decision
actions: Explain benefits (earlier detection) and harms (false-positive recall, overdiagnosis, discomfort).
Dense breasts: evidence insufficient for supplemental ultrasound or MRI (USPSTF).

clinicalManagement.title: Symptoms
actions: Do not wait for screening: refer per NICE NG12 1.4.1–1.4.3.

learningObjectives: Offer and discuss breast cancer screening for average-risk women.
